failure_case.summary: US influenza mechanism underpredicted a missed hospitalization peak.
US influenza mechanism underpredicted a missed hospitalization peak.

llm_output.why_top_candidate_wins: Chile Influenza Activity has the strongest combined evidence: it scored highest (7) and is the only candidate that simultaneously (a) is a LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR the observed target signal_us_hosp, (b) has an IMPORTATION_LINK to the mechanism eq_us_flu_base, and (c) is marked as a POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF the mechanism. This triad directly connects Chile -> mechanism -> US hospitalizations, giving a plausible causal pathway that can explain an underpredicted/missed peak (actual_above_prediction). The Australia signal lacks the IMPORTATION_LINK to the mechanism (so its influence would need to act through a different pathway), and Travel Importation Pressure lacks the LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR relation to the target (so it does not directly explain timing of the hospitalization peak). The exploratory lag evidence further supports Chile as temporally relevant: the best plausible lag within 0–16 weeks is 9 weeks with high correlation (0.8982), consistent with Chile activity arriving in time to drive a later US hospitalization peak rather than merely sharing seasonality at extremely long lags.
llm_output.proposed_minimal_edit: Add a time-lagged importation forcing term from signal_chile_flu into eq_us_flu_base with a lag parameter initialized near 9 weeks. Concretely: create or strengthen an IMPORTATION_FORCING edge signal_chile_flu --(IMPORTATION_FORCING; lag≈9wk, weight>0)--> eq_us_flu_base so the mechanism receives a lagged input from Chile activity that can increase predicted US hospitalizations.
llm_output.caveat: This recommendation is based on graph edges, candidate ranking, and exploratory lag correlation (preferencing the 9-week plausible lag). Correlation and lead/lag patterns do not prove causality; the long overall-best lag (37 weeks) suggests shared seasonality could also produce strong correlations. Test the edit empirically and compare against alternative edits (e.g., adding Australia or travel pressure inputs) and control for shared seasonal drivers before concluding causation.
